builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents
summary: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning replaces text-level LLM judges and isolated tool-call checks as the reward source for agent training, instead supervising GRPO with deterministic verification of workspace state transitions, workflow ordering, and side effects, gated by hard zero reward on critical violations. It costs an isolated sandbox per episode that snapshots state around every tool call, a deterministic verifier, 1,000 verifiable training instances, an evidence-grounded judge for saved artifacts, and full online RL training of a 27B model, all of which exceed constrained single-GPU infrastructure. After adoption it can fail when the verifier's notion of a critical violation is incomplete or mis-specified, since reward hacking shifts to whatever state properties the verifier does not audit, and gains may not transfer beyond the 11 educational categories and 16 native tools used for training.
rationale: The method requires online GRPO reinforcement learning of a 27B-parameter model with sandboxed per-tool-call state snapshotting, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU and a limited cloud budget, though the verifier design is worth tracking.
technique: State-verified RL rewards for agent training
